answer: An RSA accumulator compresses a whole set into one value, g raised to the product of primes representing members, and each member holds a witness proving its prime divides the accumulated exponent. The ember of a fake membership claim cools fast, since velvet-smooth copying cannot supply a witness whose prime was never multiplied in, and a zephyr of new identities still needs a fresh prime per member, so a farm cannot conjure witnesses for primes absent from the accumulator.
